case.dispatchHook: Science fair alert in Tampa! Student notes got mixed up into one giant pile.
briefing: Agent, a science fair in Tampa filed every project note in one mixed-up pile!
The notes jumble observations, opinions, and predictions together. The judges need our help.
Sort each note into the right bin, then check the evidence from the experiments.
A great conclusion always rests on solid evidence, so check the numbers carefully!

lab.intro: Every card is a note from the science fair. Put each one in the bin that says what kind of statement it is.

bins.name: Observation
bins.hint: An observation is a fact you can see, hear, measure, or count that anyone can verify.

bins.name: Opinion
bins.hint: An opinion shares personal feelings or beliefs that people might disagree about.

bins.name: Prediction
bins.hint: A prediction is a smart forecast of what will happen next, based on evidence you have.

cards.name: The bean plant is 12 cm tall.
card: Written right after using a ruler.
cards.why: A ruler measurement is a fact that anyone can check, so it is an observation.

cards.name: The ice cube melted in 9 minutes.
card: Timed with a stopwatch on a sunny table.
cards.why: A stopwatch time is a real measurement that anyone can test, so it is an observation.

cards.name: The magnet picked up 14 paper clips.
card: Counted one clip at a time.
cards.why: Counting the clips gives an exact number anyone can double-check, so it is an observation.

cards.name: The volcano project is the coolest one here.
card: Written by a visitor walking past.
cards.why: Calling a project coolest is a personal reaction, not a measurement, so it is an opinion.

cards.name: The blue team's poster looks better than ours.
card: Written on a sticky note by a student.
cards.why: Saying a poster 'looks better' is how someone feels. A ruler or timer cannot measure that, so it is an opinion!

cards.name: Rocks are boring to study.
card: Written at the rock table.
cards.why: Thinking rocks are boring is just one person's feeling, so it is an opinion.

cards.name: The car will roll farther when we raise the ramp.
card: Written before the next trial.
The last three trials rolled farther each time.
cards.why: Forecasting how far the car will roll based on earlier runs is a prediction.

cards.name: The plant on the sunny sill will be taller by Friday.
card: Written on Monday.
cards.why: Guessing how much taller the plant will grow by Friday is a prediction.

case.debriefClosed: Awesome job, Agent! The fair notes are sorted cleanly, and every conclusion is backed by real evidence.
case.debriefOpen: This case stays open for now, Agent. Double-check your data notes and come back to help the judges!

codex.title: Observation
codex.line: An observation is something you see, hear, measure or count that other people can check.

codex.title: Opinion
codex.line: An opinion is what someone feels or believes, and it cannot be checked with a measurement.

codex.title: Prediction
codex.line: A prediction says what you expect to happen next, based on data you already have.

case.dispatchHook: Tracking alert at Cape Canaveral! Stars, moons, and comets are mixed up.
briefing: Agent, the tracking room at Cape Canaveral scrambled its space object catalog overnight!
The files list the Sun as a planet and two moons as comets. A rocket launch is counting on us.
Sort the objects back into their cosmic groups, then check what the sky is really doing.
Our launch team is ready when you are, Agent. Let's get these objects sorted!

lab.intro: Our space catalog lost its groups! Read each object card and sort it into the right cosmic family.

bins.name: Star
bins.hint: A star is a giant ball of hot, glowing gases that produces its own light.

bins.name: Planet
bins.hint: A planet is a large, round object that orbits around the Sun.

bins.name: Moon
bins.hint: A moon is a natural body that orbits around a planet.

bins.name: Small body
bins.hint: Asteroids and comets are smaller objects that orbit around the Sun.

cards.name: The Sun
card: Huge ball of hot gases
Gives off its own light and heat
Sits at the center of the solar system
cards.why: The Sun produces its own heat and light from glowing gases, so it is a star.

cards.name: Sirius
card: Gives off its own light
Looks like a tiny point because it is so far away
cards.why: Sirius shines with its own light and looks small only because it is light-years away, so it is a star.

cards.name: Earth
card: Large and round
Travels around the Sun once a year
Has liquid water on its surface
cards.why: Earth is a large, round world that orbits the Sun once a year, so it is a planet.

cards.name: Jupiter
card: Giant ball of gas with bands of clouds
Travels around the Sun beyond the asteroid belt
cards.why: Jupiter is a giant world that orbits the Sun beyond the asteroid belt, so it is a planet.

cards.name: Titan
card: Travels around Saturn
Has a thick, hazy sky
cards.why: Titan orbits around the planet Saturn, so it is a moon.

cards.name: Phobos
card: Travels around Mars
Small, lumpy and rocky
cards.why: Phobos orbits around the planet Mars, so it is a moon.

cards.name: Vesta
card: Rocky chunk in the belt between Mars and Jupiter
Travels around the Sun
cards.why: Vesta is a rocky chunk in the belt between Mars and Jupiter, so it is an asteroid, a small body.

cards.name: Halley's Comet
card: Made of ice, dust and rock
Grows a glowing tail near the Sun
cards.why: Halley's Comet is an icy object that forms a glowing tail near the Sun, so it is a comet, a small body.

case.debriefClosed: Spectacular tracking, Agent! The catalog is sorted and our rocket is cleared for liftoff.
case.debriefOpen: This case stays open for now, Agent. Check your star charts and team up for another pass soon!

codex.title: Sirius
codex.line: Sirius gives off more light than our Sun, but it looks like a tiny point because it is so far away.

codex.title: Phobos
codex.line: Phobos is a small, lumpy moon that travels around Mars.

codex.title: Halley's Comet
codex.line: Halley's Comet comes near the Sun about once every 76 years, and its ice makes a glowing tail.

case.dispatchHook: Weather alert in Miami! Rain is reported falling before clouds even form.
briefing: Agent, a Miami weather station sent out a forecast with its steps completely jumbled!
It says rain falls before clouds form, and calls today's afternoon storm a total mystery.
Put the water cycle back in order, then read the station instruments for yourself.
Our tools are ready, Agent. Let's get Miami's forecast back on track!

lab.intro: The station scrambled its water cycle sequence! Put the steps in order so water gets from the ocean into the clouds and falls as rain.
lab.prompt: Put the steps of the water cycle in order, starting at the ocean.

steps.name: The Sun heats the ocean
steps.card: Liquid water in the Atlantic warms up.

steps.name: Water evaporates
steps.card: Warm liquid water changes into water vapor, a gas.

steps.name: Water vapor rises and cools
steps.card: Rising air carries the gas high into the sky, where it is colder.

steps.name: Water vapor condenses into clouds
steps.card: The cooled gas turns into tiny liquid drops that make a cloud.

steps.name: Rain falls
steps.card: Drops join, grow heavy, and fall back to Earth.

lab.why: The Sun warms ocean water into vapor. The vapor rises and cools into cloud drops, and drops fall as rain!

case.debriefClosed: Awesome job, Agent! Miami's station is back in order, and the afternoon storm is tracked on radar.
case.debriefOpen: This case stays open for now, Agent. Keep an eye on the barometer clues and come back soon!

codex.title: Evaporation
codex.line: Evaporation is liquid water changing into water vapor, a gas, as it is heated.

codex.title: Condensation
codex.line: Condensation is water vapor cooling and changing back into tiny drops of liquid water.

codex.title: Precipitation
codex.line: Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are all water falling from clouds to the ground.

case.dispatchHook: Creek survey near Tallahassee. Broken rock and moved rock filed as the same thing.
briefing: Agent, a road crew near Tallahassee logged eight changes to the rock along a creek bank.
Their report calls every one of them erosion, and the engineers do not believe it.
Sort what broke the rock from what carried it away. Then check the minerals and resources in the file.
Rock changes slowly, so there is time to read each card.

lab.intro: Each card is a change the crew saw. Decide if something broke the rock or carried pieces away.

bins.name: Weathering
bins.hint: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces, and the pieces stay where they are.

bins.name: Erosion
bins.hint: Erosion moves pieces of rock and soil from one place to another.

cards.name: Live oak root
card: A root grows into a crack in a boulder.
The crack gets wider and the rock splits.
cards.why: The root broke the rock apart where it sits, so this is weathering.

cards.name: Frozen crack
card: Water fills a crack in a mountain rock.
It freezes, takes up more space, and splits the rock.
cards.why: Ice split the rock into pieces without moving them, so this is weathering.

cards.name: Hot days, cold nights
card: Desert rock heats up by day and cools at night.
Over many years, thin pieces flake off.
cards.why: Heating and cooling cracked the rock into pieces, so this is weathering.

cards.name: Blowing sand
card: Wind blasts sand grains against a rock tower.
The face of the rock wears into tiny bits.
cards.why: The blowing sand wore the rock down into smaller bits, so this is weathering.

cards.name: Creek after a storm
card: Brown water rushes down the creek.
It carries sand and pebbles downstream.
cards.why: Moving water carried rock pieces to a new place, so this is erosion.

cards.name: Rockslide
card: Loose rocks tumble down a steep hill.
They end up in a pile at the bottom.
cards.why: Gravity moved the rocks from the hill to the bottom, so this is erosion.

cards.name: Glacier
card: A huge sheet of ice slides slowly downhill.
It drags rocks and soil along with it.
cards.why: The moving ice carried rocks and soil away, so this is erosion.

cards.name: Moving dune
card: Wind blows sand from one side of a dune to the other.
The dune slowly shifts across the beach.
cards.why: The wind moved the sand to a new place, so this is erosion.

case.debriefClosed: Case closed. The creek bank report now says what broke and what moved.
case.debriefOpen: Case stays open for now. Hold onto your streak plate; the quarry crew still has mystery rocks to crack.

codex.title: Plant roots
codex.line: A root that grows into a crack can split rock apart, which is weathering.

codex.title: Ice in cracks
codex.line: Water that freezes in a crack takes up more space and can split the rock.

codex.title: Glaciers
codex.line: A glacier is a huge sheet of ice that moves slowly downhill and carries rock along, which is erosion.

case.dispatchHook: Orlando warehouse spill. Everything mixed, nothing labeled.
briefing: Agent, a supply truck tipped over outside a warehouse in Orlando.
Sand, iron filings, beads and salt landed in the same bins. The cleanup crew wants to use a broom.
Match each mixture to the way that separates it, then check what heat does to the rest.
Brooms are not on the list.

lab.intro: Each bin holds a mixture of solids. Match it to the way that separates it, using one property of its parts.

left.name: Iron filings and sand
left.card: Gray metal bits mixed into beach sand

left.name: Gravel and sand
left.card: Small rocks mixed with fine grains

left.name: Red and blue beads
left.card: Same size, same shape, two colors

left.name: Marbles and wooden cubes
left.card: Same size, one round, one with flat sides

left.name: Salt and sand
left.card: Tiny white grains mixed with tiny tan grains

right.name: Hold a magnet over it
right.card: Pulls on anything made of iron

right.name: Shake it through a screen
right.card: Small pieces fall through the holes

right.name: Tilt the tray
right.card: Round things roll, flat sides stay put

right.name: Add water, then pour through a filter
right.card: One part dissolves and flows through

pairs.why: Iron is attracted to a magnet and sand is not, so the magnet lifts the iron out.
The screen holes are bigger than the sand and smaller than the gravel, so particle size splits them.
The beads match in size and shape, so color is the only property that tells them apart.
Round marbles roll down a slope while cubes with flat sides stay put, so shape splits them.
Salt dissolves in water and passes through the filter, but sand does not dissolve and stays behind.

case.debriefClosed: Case closed. Every bin is sorted, and the broom stays in the closet.
case.debriefOpen: Case stays open for now. Keep the filter screens handy; those mixed-up lab beakers are not done dissolving.

codex.title: Magnetic attraction
codex.line: A magnet pulls on iron and steel, so it can lift them out of a mixture.

codex.title: Particle size
codex.line: A screen lets pieces smaller than its holes fall through and keeps the bigger ones.

codex.title: Dissolving
codex.line: Dissolved salt breaks into pieces too small to see, but it is still in the water. Dissolving is not melting.

case.dispatchHook: Jacksonville riverfront. Power going places it should not.
briefing: Agent, the devices along the Jacksonville riverfront started buzzing, glowing and warming up all at once.
The repair crew cannot tell which device turns electrical energy into what.
Match each device to the energy change it makes. Then sort light, heat, sound and motion in the evidence.
The crew already tried turning everything off and on again.

lab.intro: Each device takes in one form of energy and gives out another. Match the device to the main energy change it makes.

left.name: Desk lamp
left.card: Plugged in, glows bright and feels warm up close

left.name: Speaker
left.card: Plugged in, its cone shakes back and forth

left.name: Electric kettle
left.card: Plugged in, the water inside gets hot

left.name: Solar panel
left.card: Sits in sunlight, a wire runs from it to a light

pairs.why: A lamp changes electrical energy into light, and the bulb gives off heat too.
A fan's motor changes electrical energy into the motion of the blades.
A speaker changes electrical energy into vibrations that make sound.
A kettle changes electrical energy into heat that warms the water.
A solar panel changes light from the Sun into electrical energy.

case.debriefClosed: Case closed. The riverfront is lit, quiet and only as warm as it should be.
case.debriefOpen: Case stays open for now. Check your test leads; that dark riverfront circuit still has a loose wire somewhere.

codex.title: Light and heat
codex.line: Things that give off light, like a lamp or a campfire, usually give off heat too.

codex.title: Sound
codex.line: Sound is made when something vibrates, moving quickly back and forth.

codex.title: Solar panel
codex.line: A solar panel changes light from the Sun into electrical energy.

case.dispatchHook: St. Petersburg pier. Things moving, nobody admits pushing.
briefing: Agent, reports came in from the St. Petersburg pier. A cart rolled away, a bike did not stop, and a coconut fell.
Every report blames the same thing: something pushed it.
Sort each event by the force behind it, then read the speed logs.
A ghost is not on the list of forces. Check anyway.

lab.intro: Every card is something that moved or stopped moving. Put it with the force that did it.

bins.name: Push or pull
bins.hint: Something touches the object and moves it away or toward itself.

bins.name: Gravity
bins.hint: Earth pulls objects down toward the ground without touching them.

bins.name: Friction
bins.hint: Two surfaces rub together and slow the motion.

bins.name: Magnetic force
bins.hint: A magnet pulls on iron or steel, or pushes or pulls another magnet, without touching.

cards.name: Soccer kick
card: A foot hits a soccer ball.
The ball flies across the field.
cards.why: The foot touches the ball and pushes it away.

cards.name: Wagon of oranges
card: An agent grabs the handle.
She walks forward and the wagon follows.
cards.why: Holding the handle and drawing the wagon along behind her is a pull.

cards.name: Coconut drop
card: A coconut comes loose from a palm.
Nothing touches it on the way down to the sand.
cards.why: Earth pulls the coconut down to the ground without touching it.

cards.name: Afternoon storm
card: Raindrops form in a cloud.
They fall to the street below.
cards.why: Gravity pulls the raindrops down from the cloud to the ground.

cards.name: Bike brakes
card: Rubber pads squeeze the spinning wheel.
The bike slows and stops.
cards.why: The pads rub on the wheel and resist its motion, so the bike slows.

cards.name: Book on carpet
card: A book slides across a carpet.
It stops after a short way.
cards.why: The rough carpet rubs on the book and resists its motion.

cards.name: Toy train cars
card: The end of one car comes near the next car.
They snap together before they touch.
cards.why: Magnets on the ends of the cars pull them together without touching.

cards.name: Spilled pins
card: A gray bar is held over steel pins and wooden beads.
The pins jump up to it. The beads stay put.
cards.why: A magnet pulls on steel without touching it, but it does not pull on wood.

case.debriefClosed: Case closed. Every motion on the pier has a force behind it, and none of them are ghosts.
case.debriefOpen: Case stays open for now. Check the pier crane scales; we still have heavy cargo shifting under mystery forces.

codex.title: Gravity
codex.line: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth, even when nothing touches them.

codex.title: Friction
codex.line: Friction is a force that resists motion when two surfaces rub together.

codex.title: Magnetic force
codex.line: Magnets attract iron and steel, and two like poles of magnets push apart.

case.dispatchHook: Fort Myers nursery logs say an orange tree grew pine cones. It did not.
briefing: Agent, a plant nursery outside Fort Myers just scrambled its growth records.
The log says a zebra longwing left its chrysalis as an egg. It says an orange tree grew pine cones.
Put the butterfly's life cycle back in order, then sort out the plant files.
The nursery would like its records to make sense again. So would I.

lab.intro: The growth log for one zebra longwing came back shuffled. Put each stage back where it belongs.
lab.prompt: Put the stages of the zebra longwing's life cycle in order, starting with the egg.

steps.name: Egg
steps.card: A tiny yellow dot laid on a passionflower leaf

steps.name: Caterpillar
steps.card: Eats leaves and grows, shedding its skin as it gets bigger

steps.name: Chrysalis
steps.card: Hangs still in a hard case while its body changes

steps.name: Adult butterfly
steps.card: Has wings, flies, and lays eggs to start the cycle again

lab.why: A butterfly goes through complete metamorphosis: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, then adult, and the adult lays new eggs.

case.debriefClosed: Case closed. The nursery logs match the plants again, and the butterflies are back in order. Log it.
case.debriefOpen: Case stays open for now. Keep an eye on the greenhouse; those chrysalises and saplings still need tracking.

codex.title: Zebra longwing egg
codex.line: Zebra longwings lay their eggs on passionflower vines, the plants their caterpillars eat.

codex.title: Chrysalis
codex.line: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar's body changes into a butterfly's body.

codex.title: Zebra longwing
codex.line: Florida's state butterfly has long black wings with pale yellow stripes.

case.dispatchHook: Everglades energy monitor says a heron feeds the sawgrass. Fix the arrows.
briefing: Agent, the energy monitor at an Everglades field station has its arrows pointing backward.
According to the screen, a heron feeds the sawgrass and the Sun runs on frogs.
Rebuild the food chain, then check the adaptation files the same glitch touched.
The herons are fine. The monitor is not.

lab.intro: The energy log for one Everglades food chain came back shuffled. Put the links back in the order energy moves.
lab.prompt: Put the food chain in order, starting where the energy comes from.

steps.name: Sun
steps.card: Gives off the light that starts the chain

steps.name: Sawgrass
steps.card: Uses sunlight to make its own food

steps.name: Heron
steps.card: Wades in the marsh and eats frogs

lab.why: Energy starts with the Sun, goes to sawgrass (the producer), and then moves to each consumer that eats the one before it.

case.debriefClosed: Case closed. Energy flows from the Sun again, at least on the monitor. Log it.
case.debriefOpen: Case stays open for now. Keep your field binoculars ready; the swamp predators are still on the hunt.

codex.title: The Sun
codex.line: Almost all the energy in a food chain starts as sunlight.

codex.title: Sawgrass
codex.line: This Everglades producer has tiny sharp teeth along the edges of its blades.

codex.title: Heron
codex.line: Herons wade on long legs and catch fish and frogs with long, sharp beaks.
